big_case.notes: The underlying question—whether federal common law or state law governs nonsignatory equitable estoppel under Chapter 2 of the FAA and the New York Convention, expressly reserved in GE Energy Power Conversion France SAS, Corp. v. Outokumpu Stainless USA, LLC, 590 U.S. 432, 445 (2020)—carries meaningful doctrinal and commercial stakes for international arbitration and the surplus-lines insurance market (particularly across dozens of post-hurricane municipal and hospital coverage disputes in Louisiana). However, this specific docket (No. 26-2) is an explicit tag-along petition seeking a hold behind the lead vehicle (Indian Harbor Insurance Co. v. Town of Vinton, No. 25-1383) and challenging a one-sentence unpublished Fifth Circuit summary affirmance, which substantially limits the standalone significance of this vehicle.
